title: How rich is Africa?
subtitle: There is no single answer: income per person in 2023 ran from $250 in Burundi to $18,131 in Seychelles.

parts.text: Africa is often described as one economy, poor and uniform. The numbers cannot be summed up in one phrase.

blocks.prompt: Think first: how many times higher do you think the richest African country's income per person is than the lowest?

parts.text: About 73 times, in 2023 World Bank figures.

items.label: the middle country of the 52 with a figure

parts.text: In 2023 gross domestic product per person, in current US dollars, was about $250 in Burundi and about $18,131 in Seychelles.
The highest is about 73 times the lowest, a ratio calculated here.
The middle country of the 52 with a figure was at about $1,709.
Eight countries were above $5,000 and sixteen below $1,000, counted here.
Eritrea and South Sudan have no figure for 2023.

blocks.title: The five highest and the five lowest
blocks.sub: GDP per person in 2023, current US dollars
blocks.note: Values are the World Bank's NY.GDP.PCAP.CD for 2023, rounded. Which countries are shown (five highest, five lowest of the 52 with a figure) is chosen here. Eritrea and South Sudan have no 2023 figure.

parts.text: GDP per person divides a country's total output by its population. It does not say how income is shared, what things cost, or how much work happens outside the market.
It is a starting point for asking questions, not a verdict on any place.

gaps: GDP per capita in current US dollars depends on exchange rates, so it can move without anyone's life changing. Other measures, such as purchasing-power comparisons, give a different spread and are not used here.
The summary figures are our own arithmetic on one year's World Bank values; a different year would change them.
Nothing here covers inequality inside countries, which can be as wide as the gap between them.

keyPoints.text: In 2023 income per person ran from about $250 in Burundi to about $18,131 in Seychelles.
The highest is about 73 times the lowest; the middle country of the 52 with a figure was at about $1,709.
GDP per person is a starting point for questions, not a verdict on any place.
